subject: paediatrics
title: Duct-Dependent Lesions, Prostaglandin E1 and Blalock-Taussig Shunt

steps.tx: Critical neonatal survival frequently relies upon maintaining fetal vascular conduits before definitive surgery. Specific complex anomalies are classified as **duct-dependent congenital heart lesions**, where systemic or pulmonary blood flow depends entirely on flow through a patent ductus arteriosus. In duct-dependent pulmonary lesions like pulmonary atresia or severe tetralogy, spontaneous ductal closure precipitates fatal asphyxia and profound metabolic acidosis.
steps.say: Duct-dependent heart lesions require an open ductus arteriosus to survive. Spontaneous ductal closure in pulmonary atresia cuts off lung perfusion, leading to fatal hypoxia.

steps.tx: Targeted physiological classification separates duct-dependent lesions based on the endangered circulatory bed. Lesions are categorized into **duct-dependent pulmonary blood flow** (pulmonary atresia, critical pulmonary stenosis, tricuspid atresia, severe tetralogy) and duct-dependent systemic blood flow (hypoplastic left heart syndrome, critical aortic coarctation, interrupted aortic arch). Maintaining ductal patency is mandatory in both categories to preserve life prior to catheter or surgical intervention.
steps.say: Duct-dependent lesions divide into those needing ductal flow for the lungs, like pulmonary atresia, and those needing it for the body, like hypoplastic left heart syndrome.

rows: Pulmonary atresia, critical PS, severe TOF
Shunts aorta -> pulmonary artery to oxygenate
Severe cyanosis and hypoxic cardiac arrest
Shunts PA -> aorta to perfuse kidneys and body

steps.tx: Continuous intravenous infusion of synthetic prostaglandin maintains ductal smooth muscle relaxation. The immediate life-saving medical emergency therapy is **intravenous prostaglandin E1 alprostadil**, administered at a starting dose of 0.01 to 0.05 micrograms per kilogram per minute. Alprostadil directly relaxes vascular smooth muscle in the ductus arteriosus within thirty minutes, restoring pulmonary or systemic blood flow and correcting metabolic acidosis.
steps.say: Intravenous prostaglandin E1 directly relaxes ductal smooth muscle, reopening the ductus within thirty minutes to restore perfusion. The starting dose is 0.01 to 0.05 micrograms per kilogram per minute.

left.title: Prostaglandin E1 Therapeutic Action
points: Relaxes ductal circular smooth muscle
Dramatically re-opens constricting ductus within 30 min
Corrects metabolic lactic acidosis and hypoxaemia
Stabilizes neonate for diagnostic echocardiography

right.title: Prostaglandin E1 Adverse Effects
points: Sudden apnoea occurs in 10 to 12% of neonates
Readiness for immediate endotracheal intubation
Peripheral cutaneous flushing and peripheral vasodilation
Drug-induced hyperpyrexia and hypotension

steps.tx: Palliative systemic-to-pulmonary artery shunting establishes reliable pulmonary perfusion until total repair. The primary palliative surgical procedure is the **modified Blalock-Taussig shunt**, which interposes a synthetic polytetrafluoroethylene (Gore-Tex) vascular tube graft between the subclavian artery (or innominate artery) and the ipsilateral branch pulmonary artery. This provides calibrated pulmonary blood flow, allowing the pulmonary arterial tree to grow while avoiding cardiopulmonary bypass.
steps.say: The modified Blalock-Taussig shunt places a Gore-Tex tube graft from the subclavian to the pulmonary artery. It delivers reliable pulmonary blood flow until total repair is possible.

rows: Gore-Tex tube graft subclavian to PA
Gore-Tex tube ascending aorta to main PA
Used when subclavian arteries are small
Higher risk of excessive pulmonary flow
Ascending aorta to right pulmonary artery
Difficult to take down; causes distortion

steps.tx: Sizing the synthetic prosthetic graft balances adequate oxygenation against pulmonary vascular flood. The diameter of the **Gore-Tex shunt graft** is chosen according to infant body weight: 3.0 millimetres for neonates under three kilograms, and 3.5 millimetres for neonates weighing three to four kilograms. An undersized shunt causes persistent cyanosis and hypoxia, while an oversized graft causes excessive pulmonary runoff, pulmonary edema, systemic hypoperfusion, and necrotizing enterocolitis.
steps.say: A 3.0 or 3.5 millimetre Gore-Tex graft provides calibrated blood flow based on weight. Undersized shunts leave the infant cyanotic, while oversized grafts cause pulmonary edema.

left.title: Undersized Shunt Risks
points: Persistent cyanosis with SpO2 <75%
Metabolic acidosis and poor exercise tolerance
Early thrombotic occlusion of narrow graft lumen
Requires emergency shunt revision or dilation

right.title: Oversized Shunt Risks
points: Excessive pulmonary blood flow (Qp:Qs >3:1)
Pulmonary edema and ventilator dependence
Systemic steal syndrome dropping diastolic BP
Necrotizing enterocolitis and renal failure

steps.tx: Auscultation confirms uninterrupted graft patency through both phases of the cardiac cycle. Successful functioning of a Blalock-Taussig shunt is confirmed by hearing a **continuous soft shunt murmur** beneath the clavicle on the operative side. Sudden disappearance of this continuous murmur accompanied by acute central cyanosis indicates acute thrombotic occlusion of the prosthetic graft, requiring immediate systemic heparinization, emergent catheter thrombolysis, or surgical exploration.
steps.say: Hearing a continuous soft murmur beneath the clavicle confirms that the Blalock-Taussig shunt is working. Sudden disappearance of the murmur with severe cyanosis signals acute shunt thrombosis.

rows: Catheter tPA infusion or emergency stent

steps.tx: Staged single-ventricle palliation diverts systemic venous blood directly into the lungs without a subpulmonary pump. In univentricular hearts where biventricular repair is impossible (e.g. tricuspid atresia, hypoplastic left heart), initial neonatal shunt palliation is followed at four to six months by the **bidirectional Glenn anastomosis**. The superior vena cava is anastomosed end-to-side to the right pulmonary artery, unloading the single ventricle and delivering passive upper-body venous flow.
steps.say: The bidirectional Glenn anastomosis connects the superior vena cava directly to the pulmonary artery at four to six months. This unloads the single ventricle and delivers passive upper-body venous flow.

left.title: Stage 2: Bidirectional Glenn (4-6 Months)
points: SVC anastomosed to right pulmonary artery
Provides stable passive upper-body blood flow
Unloads volume workload on single ventricle
Takes down previous neonatal systemic shunt

right.title: Stage 3: Completed Fontan (2-4 Years)
points: IVC flow diverted to pulmonary artery via conduit
Separates systemic and pulmonary venous blood
Complete resolution of arterial cyanosis (SpO2 >95%)
Passive non-pulsatile pulmonary blood flow

steps.tx: Long-term surveillance tracks pulmonary arterial growth and branching geometry. As children with systemic-to-pulmonary shunts grow, serial **echocardiography and cardiac catheterization** assess McGoon ratio and Nakata index to ensure symmetrical growth of branch pulmonary arteries without anastomotic stenosis or distortion. Adequate branch pulmonary vessel development is mandatory before proceeding to complete corrective repair of tetralogy or completion of the Fontan circulation.
steps.say: Serial echocardiography monitors pulmonary artery growth and excludes shunt stenosis. Adequate branch pulmonary artery size is mandatory before definitive surgical correction.

rows: Cross-sectional area of branch PAs / BSA
Confirms adequacy for total TOF repair
Sum of branch PA diameters / Diaphragm aorta
Indicates sufficient vascular bed for bypass
